bill_title: H.R. 1968, Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act
corrections: date and tally, both from the AFL-CIO's own page, and the printed date is IMPOSSIBLE rather than merely unmatched: it publishes 'February 20, 2025', and the HOUSE did not pass H.R. 1968 until 11 March 2025 (rolls 68-69), so the measure had not reached the Senate on 20 February. Every Senate roll call on it falls on 14 March, and its only passage vote is roll 133 at 54-46, which is what the record's 'Passed' describes. The printed 51-49 belongs to nothing on this measure - the 2025 Senate's only 51-49s are the Patel nomination and an S.Con.Res. 7 amendment, both on 20 February. CONFIRMED 31 Aug 2026 by the scorecard's own per-legislator export, which settles WHERE the wrong key came from: this record's column of marks reproduces roll 70 - the S.Con.Res. 7 amendment of 20 February, 51-49 - EXACTLY, on all 100 senators, while roll 133 leaves 5 wrong. So the site linked the record to roll 70 and took its date, its tally and its member marks from there. The intent is not in doubt: the AFL-CIO's own legislative alert attached to this record is dated 13 March 2025 and opposes 'the Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025 (H.R. 1968) scheduled for Senate floor consideration this week'. The match stands; the export column is the defective artifact. Date 2025-02-20 -> 2025-03-14 and tally 51-49 -> 54-46; date 2025-02-20 -> 2025-03-14 per Voteview roll 133; tally 51-49 -> 54-46 per Voteview roll 133
